items.summary: The government holds these consultations annually to gather input from experts and industry representatives before finalising Budget priorities and proposals.

items.title: Verify legal status of educational institutions before taking admission: UGC tells students
items.summary: The University Grants Commission has issued an advisory regarding the verification of educational institutions. In the advisory, it emphasizes the need to check the legitimacy of institutions before enrolling. Students and parents should independently confirm the claims made by institutions through official sources. The UGC highlights the importance of ensuring recognition and approval from relevant authorities. This guidance aims to prevent financial and academic mishaps for prospective students.

items.title: Piyush Goyal, Italy's Tajani seek stronger ties in autos, pharma and technology
items.summary: India and Italy are fostering stronger economic ties through joint ventures and technology partnerships. They seek collaboration in sectors such as automotive, aerospace, and agriculture. The discussions took place during the recent India-Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation meeting in Rome. Participants highlighted the importance of investment partnerships and technology sharing for successful outcomes. Both countries aim to integrate into global value chains effectively.

items.title: India-US FTA could strengthen aerospace partnerships, boost business opportunities: Gautam Singhania
items.summary: Gautam Singhania emphasized the potential benefits of the proposed India-US Free Trade Agreement for aerospace partnerships. He noted that his company, Raymond Aerospace, has long-standing relationships with American firms. The 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit facilitated networking opportunities to strengthen commercial ties between both nations. Various industry representatives explored collaboration possibilities that could benefit both sides. Increased cooperation in aerospace could lead to growth in business opportunities through this trade agreement.

items.title: Lower crude prices, higher diesel cracks restore profitability of oil marketing companies in Q2FY27: Report
items.summary: India's oil marketing companies including IOC, BPCL, and HPCL returned to profitability in the second quarter of FY27. This recovery followed a period of losses in the previous quarter and was supported by lower crude oil prices. Additionally, a rise in diesel refining margins and an increase in pump prices contributed to improved earnings. However, BPCL experienced a weaker recovery compared to the other companies during this period.

items.title: EU delays methane emission rules on fossil fuel imports
items.summary: New rules will not be implemented for at least two years after sustained lobbying by US, Qatar and oil and gas sector

items.title: New PUC certificate validity rules notified: What vehicle owners need to know
items.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has announced new rules regarding the validity of Pollution Under Control certificates. These revisions cater to vehicles based on emission standards and age, affecting renewal timelines. For example, BS-VI compliant vehicles will have longer validity compared to older standards. Furthermore, the rules specify how renewals will be processed and when they take effect.

items.title: Wedding bells and travel demand ring in for India's hotels
items.summary: India's hotel industry is projecting healthy revenue growth supported by a strong wedding calendar in 2027. Revenue per available room rose significantly in October due to increased domestic travel and various events. While some growth may moderate due to a favorable base effect, the recovery in foreign tourists is crucial. Bengaluru and Hyderabad showed the highest RevPAR growth in October among major cities.

items.title: FCNR-related costs and benefits yet to fully play out for banks: Report
items.summary: Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits are expected to significantly influence the performance of Indian banks. The benefits and costs associated with these deposits have not fully materialized for financial institutions. Banks exhibiting a strong position in fixed-rate FCNR deposits may manage rising funding costs more effectively. Variations in loan growth and deposit composition among banks could lead to different performance outcomes.

items.title: Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019
items.summary: Takaichi received a subdued welcome on her trip to attend the APEC summit, as Beijing shows limited appetite for repairing ties strained by Taiwan dispute.

items.title: Blackstone-backed Aster DM in talks to acquire rival hospitals in deeper India push
items.summary: Aster DM Quality Care Ltd. is currently in discussions to purchase hospitals from Narayana Hrudayalaya Ltd. The deal is valued at approximately $150 million and could enhance Aster DM's market position. Interest in consolidation within India's healthcare sector has surged among private equity investors in recent years. Blackstone, which has a significant investment in Aster DM, views the company as a key global asset.

items.title: Saudi Arabia overtakes UAE as India's No. 2 oil supplier; Russia retains lead
items.summary: India's oil imports from Saudi Arabia rose significantly in October, exceeding those from the UAE. Saudi imports reached approximately 790,000 barrels per day, while UAE imports fell to 612,000 barrels per day. This shift occurred after the Iran war disrupted regional supplies and caused competition among Gulf producers. Indian refiners increased Russian oil purchases sharply as well amid changing market dynamics.

items.title: Rising commodity costs hit passenger vehicle makers harder than two-wheeler companies: Jefferies
items.summary: Rising commodity costs are significantly impacting the profitability of passenger vehicle manufacturers compared to two-wheeler companies. Two-wheeler manufacturers have demonstrated better efficiency in converting revenue growth into profits despite cost pressures. In contrast, passenger vehicle companies are facing downgrades in their earnings estimates. The automobile sector is also dealing with a high volume base expected later in FY27.

items.title: Gilts v kilts: What is happening with Scottish government bonds?
items.summary: MSPs have heard both the pros and cons of the government's plan to launch its first ever bond to the market.

items.title: Mideast crisis 'largest threat' to energy security ever: IEA
items.summary: The crisis in the Middle East sparked in February by the US and Israeli bombing of Iran has created the "largest threat" to energy security in history, the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned Thursday. "The Strait of Hormuz crisis has created the largest threat to energy security in history, one that dwarfs the scale of the oil shocks of the 1970s," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol wrote in his foreword to the report.

items.title: India’s top infrastructure financier plans foray in ABS market
items.summary: NaBFID is preparing to enter the asset-backed securities market next year as both issuer and investor. The move aims to diversify funding sources and support India's infrastructure finance needs, which are substantial. India's securitization market is growing rapidly, having increased by nearly 42% recently, attracting global investments.

items.title: Jaishankar meets senior Japanese leaders; discusses deeper strategic, economic ties
items.summary: S Jaishankar met with key Japanese leaders in Tokyo to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation. The focus was on enhancing strategic, economic, and energy security ties between India and Japan. In addition, Jaishankar will co-chair the upcoming India-Japan 2+2 Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue. This dialogue aims to review various aspects of defense cooperation and relations. Both nations maintain a Special Strategic and Global Partnership encompassing multiple areas of collaboration.

items.title: Maharashtra leads passenger vehicle sales, UP tops two-and three-wheelers
items.summary: Maharashtra recorded the highest passenger vehicle sales with 1,65,000 units in the July-September quarter. Uttar Pradesh led in two-wheeler sales with 7,89,000 units, accounting for 12.3% of total sales. The total passenger vehicle sales in India reached 13.61 lakh units during this period. The western region dominated in three of the four segments of vehicle sales. The southern region led in three-wheelers with a total of 96,000 units sold.

items.title: UK inflation hits one-year high of 3.6%: Why are markets less convinced of another rate hike? | Explained
items.summary: UK inflation rose to a one-year high of 3.6% in October, driven by higher fuel prices and tobacco taxes. However, unchanged core and services inflation eased market expectations of a Bank of England rate hike in December, despite concerns over rising energy costs and future price pressures.

items.title: Vedanta Group explores using AI in complex mineral production
items.summary: The group said that it is exploring the use of artificial intelligence for geological analysis and mineral block modelling, which could potentially reduce exploration timelines from 3-4 months to just 6-7 days.

items.title: Tata Sons board members including Chandrasekaran, Noel Tata to visit Air India HQ for performance review
items.summary: Tata Sons board members will visit Air India headquarters in Gurugram to discuss the airline's performance and strategies. The airline has faced challenges including rising fuel costs and operational issues. Air India's MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam will present on the airline's transformation efforts. Noel Tata has expressed concerns regarding Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman amidst these challenges.

items.title: India-New Zealand FTA to cut wine tariffs from 150% to 25-50% over 10 years
items.summary: India will gradually lower wine tariffs on New Zealand imports, which currently stand at 150%. This reduction is part of the new India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, expected to last for ten years. New Zealand companies are optimistic about expanding their market presence in India. Both countries anticipate mutual benefits from this trade deal in various sectors. An increase in wine consumption in India may follow these tariff reductions.

items.title: India on track to hit $1 trillion exports target in FY27: Commerce Secretary
items.summary: India's exports increased by 16.6% in the first half of this fiscal year. The country aims to reach $1 trillion in exports by 2026-27. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal stated that India is on track to meet this goal. Despite global trade uncertainties, India continues to be viewed positively as a trusted trading partner. India achieved record exports of $863 billion in the previous fiscal year.

items.title: Ahmedabad crash: Final investigation report likely soon, Centre tells Supreme Court
items.summary: The investigation into the Air India crash in Ahmedabad that occurred in June 2025 is nearing completion. The Solicitor General has requested a brief adjournment of the court proceedings of two to three weeks. An independent investigation has been sought by the families of the victims and an NGO. The final report will be submitted in a sealed cover, following international protocols.

items.title: RBI warns Yes Bank AT1 bond ruling could weaken future bank rescue framework
items.summary: The case relates to Yes Bank's rescue in 2020, when authorities wrote off Rs 8,415 crore worth of additional Tier-1 (AT1) bonds. These securities are designed to absorb losses when banks face financial distress.

items.title: India, US close to finalising trade deal talks, signing may take time
items.summary: The trade deal negotiations between India and the US are nearing completion, according to Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal. He stated that the legal texts are almost finalized. However, the signing hinges on the establishment of new US tariff rules and the resolution of ongoing Section 301 investigations.
